Report Details

Violation ID: 875638
Permit API: 039-25764
Unconventional: Yes
County: Crawford
Municipality: East Fallowfield Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-01-31
Comments: Follow-up inspection to check brine spill cleanup and containment issues at frac tank used for production water containment. Contaminated material has been collected and is inside a lined roll-off dumpster on site. Limestone from elsewhere on the site has been added to the excavated area from cleanup. Frac tank has been removed from original liner and is placed on a temporary liner on site. A new, properly sized liner is scheduled to be delivered and installed on 2/3/20. No personnel on site. WQS and operator have not yet discussed well site restoration violations pertaining to ESCGP permit. Awaiting written response from operator regarding Notice of Violation. Comments from previous inspection noted below: Inspection related to cleanup of brine and oil inside the liner which is used as secondary containment for the stock tank (old frac tank); see photo 1. The tank has overflowed/over-sprayed from a thief hatch or access door. A Pin Oak Energy employee and two-man crew from Diamond Energy Partners has vac-trucked brine/oil from the liner. Some oil/paraffin and brine still remains in the liner. During the cleanup, brine has leaked out of a hole in the bottom of the liner and flowed onto the soil-cement stabilized limestone pad. As of Monday, 1/27/20, some of the affected limestone has been placed in a roll-off on site. Clean up will continue on 1/28/20 to remove contaminated material from under the liner, and correct the secondary containment issues. Contaminated material on the well pad needs removed/remediated. Also, all contamination needs removed from within the secondary containment. SWMA violations noted for discharge of residual waste (brine) to ground. Site restoration violations are also cited in this Notice of Violation. The well site has not been restored to post-construction stage.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-06-25 to William H Brawand in Jones Twp, Elk county. 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: William H Brawand
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-06-25
Violation Code: 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 853698
Permit API: 047-25054
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-06-25
Comments: While drilling on 6/24, the operator encountered fresh water. Cement returns and drill cuttings ran down the location toward a stream. The operator dug two small pits to contain this water and solids in order to prevent discharge to the stream. Some of the dirt was pushed right to the edge of the stream. Rain overnight 6/24-25 allowed the pits to overflow and also caused sediment to run into the stream from the location and dirt piles. At the time of this inspection, the stream and pits were both colored with sediment, which could also be seen in a pond just downstream. Drilling will continue 6/26-27, after which the drilling contractor will empty the pits and backfill. It was suggested that they pump the water as far from the stream as possible and/or use a sediment filter bag to prevent any further discharge.

CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DANNIC ENERGY CORP
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/28/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8215158
Permit API: 033-25741
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Huston Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/28/2025
Comments: Routine site inspection at conventional well 033-25741 on January 28, 2025. The well site was snow covered. The well appears active and capable of producing. Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected. Please note, a small hole was observed on the back side of the brine tank (pictures 4 and 5). No visible fluids were observed trickling out of the hole, but the tank appears full up to that hole. No visible fluids were observed on the ground in the snow but there is evidence that the tank has been leaking. Orange staining was observed from the brine leak, there is an indentation in the ground directly below the leak, and a path of deer tracks lead up to the leaking brine tank. Please note, that I was unable to collect a soil sample due to frozen conditions. Violations have been cited.

Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. Onsite with DEP staff Alicia Furey and Lucas Eichner to collect a water sample from the earthen dike. The earthen dike is retaining fluid inside the bottom of the entire dike. There is approximately 4-5" of oily water pooled inside the dike. The dike drain remains closed and plugged. Water flowing into a separator barrel on top of a steel oil tank could be heard from the ground.Prior to the site visit water samples of the Bellows Spring was collected for analysis. There are 4 separate pipes flowing water into the cistern for the spring. Each pipe was identified, labeled, and sampled separately.After collecting samples from the earthen dike, DEP staff walked the hillside between the tank battery and Bellows Spring. The goal was to investigate any other oil and gas activity that may be located above the spring and that would be a potential contributor to the impact of the Bellows Spring. There was nothing observed between the tank battery and the Bellows Spring relating to oil and gas activity.At 2:05pm Mr. Rhoades was called via phone by the Department. The current condition of the tank battery was discussed with Mr. Rhoades and he indicated that a water truck is scheduled for next week to empty the dike and the brine tanks. Mr. Rhoades also stated that he has hired Moody and Associates as a consultant and that a check was in the mail to obtain their services. The Department clearly communicated the importance and urgency of starting the cleanup process at the site including the earthen dike area. Mr. Rhoades seemed to understand and asked if the water was good to drink yet in Reno and if individual households are being tested. I explained to Mr. Rhoades that samples have been taken from the spring by Oil and Gas Operations and that I was unaware of any other sampling/testing. It was also stated that the "Do not Consume" advisory has not yet been lifted from my knowledge at the time. The phone call was concluded with Mr. Rhoades indicating that he is starting the process to clean things up.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/15/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Brokenstraw Township, Warren county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/15/2026
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8278406
Permit API: 123-45905
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Brokenstraw Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/15/2026
Comments: A discharge of production fluids is evident at the Conklin Lease tank battery. Mature trees at the southwest corner of the secondary containment area are either heavily stressed or dead. A brine tank is buried within the secondary containment area. PVC lines connect the drain valves of the stock tanks in containment to cutout holes in the surface of the brine tank. Evidence of previous fluid releases in the containment area are visible via crude oil staining and sawdust sprinkled over the oil-stained areas. It appears that the PVC lines connected to the two stock tanks in the southernmost end of the containment area have been the most heavily used. At the time of this inspection, the PVC lines are placed inside the cutout holes of the brine tank. However, oil-staining, visible wetness, and sawdust sprinkled around these cutout holes indicate that at one time fluid was allowed to run over the surface of the brine tank and onto the ground within the secondary containment area. Elevated specific conductance in soils in excess of 3,000 uS/cm was observed beneath both of the aforementioned PVC lines.A pool of fluid was present in the southernmost end of the containment area, in what appeared to be a sump. At the time of this inspection, the fluid was observed to have elevated specific conductance exceeding 4,000 uS/cm. Soils at the bottom of the sump also had elevated specific conductance which measured in excess of 11,000 uS/cm. The floor of the secondary containment area above the sump was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 uS/cm. A drainage swale is located approximately 30 feet west of the secondary containment area wall. Upslope soil conductivity readings in the swale were observed at 96 uS/cm. Elevated specific conductance in excess of 4,000 uS/cm was observed in soils within the swale directly across from the tank battery. Crude oil staining was also observed in the swale near the tank battery. The swale transitions to an UNT to Irvine Run with defined bed and banks downslope of the tank battery. The water flowing in the UNT was found to have elevated specific conductance exceeding 13,000 uS/cm. Elevated specific conductance of water was observed throughout the stream at the time of this inspection. The specific conductance of water in the stream was observed to drop below 1,000 uS/cm after two confluences with apparently unaffected sources of fresh water at a point approximately 200 feet north of a culvert and the lease road which crosses the UNT. Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with brine disposal receipts for the Conklin lease.

Code §78a.86, which provides: ¿In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under § 78a.91 ¿ 78a.98 (related to plugging).¿ Therefore, please provide a written response within 30 days of receipt of this Notice of Violation, as to when and how the above listed violations were or will be corrected, and what steps are being taken to prevent their recurrence.

Violation Code: 78.64(d)2 - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator drained tank containment facilities without responsible supervision and failed to follow proper drainage procedure.
Violation ID: 8153360
Permit API: 121-45433
Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Sugarcreek Borough
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/21/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023.There is an active discharge of fluid from the Tank Battery of the Lower Reno oil lease that is permitted and operated by Petro Erie Inc.. The public water supply for the town of Reno, PA is under a "Do Not Consume Advisory" based upon an increase in TDS for the Bellows Spring Cistern (owned and operated by Venango Water Company).The tank battery consists of (2) 210bbl steel tanks and (4) 100bbl poly tanks. The earthen dike appears to be lined with a plastic liner. There is a dike drain that is located in the southwest corner of the dike. The valve on the drain pipe is open and fluid is flowing to the ground. The area inside the dike appears to have been impacted by produced fluid from the tanks. A pipeline between two of the poly tanks was actively dripping fluid. Field screening inside the dike were conducted with the soil probe for conductivity, and all readings were above the range of the meter (20,000uS).The discharge from the dike drain flows south across an open area and into a wooded area. There is a visible impact area extending from the dike drain in an irregular pattern approximately 80 yards from the earthen dike and approximately ranging from 6' to 25' in width. Field screening within the impacted area was conducted approximately every 10 yards. Conductivity measurements ranged from 11,000uS to above the range of the meter (20,000uS). Several areas outside of the impacted area were checked with the soil probe and the levels ranged between 60uS to 164uS. An oil sheen is visible within the flowing water and dead vegetation is also observed including several large cherry trees within the impacted area. The amount of discharged fluid is unknown and based upon the observations onsite it appears that the discharge has been occurring for some time.The dike drain was closed by DEP staff at 8:45am to stop the continued discharge of fluid outside of the earthen dike.Water samples were collected at the dike drain outlet (discharge point) and sent to the lab for analysis. Water samples were also collected at the Bellows Spring Cistern (41.422360 -79.764490) which is a source for a public water supply of the town of Reno, PA.While onsite the Department talked with the operator/owner (Harry Rhoades) via a phone conversation. The discharge and the potential that the discharge may be impacting the public water supply was discussed with Mr. Rhoades. Mr. Rhoades insisted that he does not discharge his brine and that he could provide disposal documents. It was stated that the dike drain was left open because of forecasted rain. Violations are cited.The Oil and Gas Inspector (OGI) will be conducting a separate well compliance inspection for the well and other wells on the lease.

Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted to document a field review of the recent removal of grub material previously located between the proposed Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads. William Cenk and Brian Bennett of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) were present for the duration of this inspection. Brian Ayers (WQSS) and I, Mathew Haemer (WQS), were present to represent the Department.During the 07/21/26 JPA pre-application meeting between TMP and the Department, Department Technical Services staff requested that the grub material placed south of the roadway between the Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads be removed as soon as possible to potentially restore the hydrology near the road and well pad construction back to its original condition. It was observed that the grub material had impeded and redirected the flow of an Unnamed Tributary to Jackson Run and had begun to cause E and S problems alongside the roadway, well pad, and below the well pad for the proposed Akins #4 conventional well.At the time of this inspection, it appeared that all of the grub material had been removed as requested. However, TMP had also elected to redefine one of the stream channels below the well pad for Akins #3 and direct its flow through the disturbed area south of the roadway to Akins #4. The excavation work related to this stream channel continues to cause erosion and sedimentation to occur alongside the roadway and well pad for the proposed Akins #4. This is not the outcome Technical Services staff intended to result from the removal of the grub material. At the time of this inspection, the newly excavated stream channel is unprotected from erosion. There are three filter socks installed south of the Akins #4 well pad beyond the excavated stream channel directly in line with this channelized flow. Filter sock is not designed to be installed in channelized flow. All three filter socks are being undercut by the channelized flow. Evidence of erosion and sedimentation is still present before and after each filter sock. The area south and continuing west of Akins #4 that is now accepting the flow of this stream water is beginning to erode. A forested wetland is located west and down grade from the Akins #4 well pad. Bank erosion and saturated earth below the wetland indicate that the stream water overflows the wetland during storm events.The Department has yet to receive an updated E and S Plan that meets the expectations of the Technical Services staff. It is recommended that no further earth disturbance occurs without notification to and approval by the Department.The encroachment violations and violations relating to erosion and sediment control continue in the present condition of this construction and related excavation work.The violation for failure to post the well permit during construction has been closed.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/08/2023
Comments: On February 8, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection at the Kiskiminetas Spring School 4 well in Loyalhanna Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3488724, where high conductivity was found underneath the brine tank valve. The Department had yet to receive the waste manifest from remediation or the quantity released in the spill noted in IR 3307023, therefore the Department was unable to assess whether the spill had been remediated in accordance with DEP Spill Policy. Violations were continued as a result, and the Department requested that the operator provide the waste manifest and any other relevant information no later than February 10, 2023. Heavy tire rutting was also observed on the access road. Present were myself, DEP OGI Curtis Small, Brian Haney from PA Mineral Services, and Joe Miller from Mid Atlantic Energy Services. The following was observed:The well site appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no concerns related to E and S or vegetative coverage (see photo 7). The API number and operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 4). This information now reflects the information that the Department has on file. A hissing sound and a strong gas odor was observed coming from the well head at the time of inspection (see photo 5). Mr. Haney and Mr. Miller were making repairs on the well head at the time of inspection. The brine tank appeared to be sound at the time of inspection (see photo 3). However, elevated conductivity remains underneath the brine tank valve (see photo 1). A background soil conductivity reading was taken along the access road, which read 120 Microsiemens (see photo 9). Heavy tire rutting remains in the access road (see photo 8). It was initially noted that the access road is shared with the operator and Kiski Prep School. However, Mr. Haney informed the Department that unrelated timber trucks also use the access road for removal of trees for timber. Trees that are said to be marked for timber use could be observed north of the well site (see photo 6).Based on observations from this inspection, the the Department recommends that the operator investigate the cause of the elevated conductivity and remediate accordingly. Violations remain outstanding. The Department also recommends that the operator cooperatively monitor and maintain the access road with Kiski School, and Timber companies that use it to prevent accelerated erosion. The Department requests that the operator provide the waste manifest and any other relevant information, including quantity released no later than February 10, 2023.

Comments: The operator reported to DEP on 7/10/19 that a 1-2 barrel spill of production fluid occurred at the E09 S well pad. This inspection occurred the morning of 7/11. It appears as though a fitting on a dump line from a bulk unit failed, which allowed produced water to spill into the containment within the unit. Once the containment of approximately 600 gallons was filled, water began to spill out on either side of the unit. Workers on site noticed the spill and immediately shut the site down so that containment and remediation could begin. It is estimated that 1-2 barrels of production fluid was spilled to the ground. Equipment was brought to the site and three roll-off containers were filled with contaminated soil. The operator used a soil probe to determine where conductivity was elevated and dug an area approximately 30x60 feet at the time of this inspection. They did not dig under the bulk unit, as they were going to attempt to flush any production fluid out from under it rather than move the unit at this time. Work will continue on this site until soil tests come back clean. No threats to nearby water sources were noted, as this spill was contained within a small area on the pad.

Comments: On 04/07/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLCs Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1045 hours, weather was 34F and cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Standing water observed on the pad surface field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of ~310-332us/cm.There are 2 recently completed wells located onsite; the well permits are posted at the site entrance, however, I did not observe any tags on the wells (photo #2). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #3). The GPUs are held in a secondary containment structure which contained less than 10% standing water. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #4); the containment structure contained less than 10% standing water. A dehydration unit is also noted onsite and is held in secondary containment (photo #5).Numerous temporary storage tanks are noted onsite for ongoing flow back activities, these tanks are held in secondary containment structures which retain sufficient storage capacity (photos #6 and 7). 6 upright brine storage tanks are also noted onsite but are not held in secondary containment (photo #8). 2 residual waste containers were also observed not held in secondary containment (photo #9).Perennial vegetative cover continues to grow in the areas surrounding the site (photo #10). No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. A weekly erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review and is up to date (photo #11). 1 infiltration basin serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photos #12). No standing water was observed in the PCSM control and it appears to be functioning as intended.The DEP recommends the following:-Installing well tags on the wellheads. -Placing the upright brine storage tanks in secondary containment if they still contain a regulated substance to prevent violations from being cited against 25 PA 78a57(c).-Placing the residual waste containers in secondary containment.Violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962 pending receipt of confirmation sampling and approval of Act 2 remediation standards.No additional violations noted. I departed the site at 1045 hours.

Comments: On July 10, 2025, the Department conducted a Routine Complete Inspection of Monona's Stickle 1H well site located in Fairfield Township, Westmoreland County. Accompanying on today's inspection is Tyler Metzger (WQS DEP).At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Act 9 sign at the access road entrance to not be in compliance, the Department recommends the Operator replace the Act 9 Sign with one that satisfies 78a55(i)4ii. In the on-site mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan, however it had a different Operator's name posted on it, the Department recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well site perimeters appeared to be exhibiting at last 70% uniform and adequate vegetative cover.At the time of this inspection, the Stickle 1H well site appeared to have 2 wells on it, the 1H (permit number 129-28411) had a well tag fixed to the wellhead with the well's name and permit number on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead.A plethora of production equipment that did not appear to equipped for production was observed in several locations of the well site, the Department recommends all equipment not currently in use be removed from the well site.2 production tanks were observed to be within a secondary containment that had a minimal amount of fluid pooled in it as well as an unlabeled barrel. The production tanks appeared to be heavily corroded with several holes observed at the top of the tank located on the right-hand side. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the structural integrity of the production tanks to ensure further corrosion and a release of production fluids does not occur. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed several areas of the graveled well pad to have an oily substance on it, specifically in areas relating to the reported re-plugging of the 129-28648 well. Violations were issued against the 129-28648 well for a release(s) of an oily substance.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the Act 9 Sign not in compliance, the outdated ERP and for the corrosion holes in the production tank.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/25/2023 at 0820 hours. The weather was 38 degrees with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted to summarize recent remedial activities since the last follow-up inspection on 4/10/2023 regarding a release from 4/6/2023. Blackhill has now had the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment structure removed from the impacted area. All material in this area that Blackhill discovered to have elevated electrical conductivity (EC) has been excavated (photos #1 and 2) and placed within lined waste containers or on secondary containment and covered (photo #3). I field measured water collected in the accessible portions of the excavated area shown in photos #1 and 2 and received readings of ~1.7mS/cm. Blackhill continues to have water that collects in these areas pumped out. The produced water tanks have been moved to a new location along the northern edge of the pad with a new secondary containment structure (photo #7). The yellow bin that holds the offload valve has now been placed further back so the entire bin is within secondary containment. Blackhill reported that elevated EC water was discovered along the buried produced water flowline. Portions of the pad material where the flowline was buried have now been excavated to a point where it can be done safely. The buried produced water flowline closest to the processing equipment has been "pot-holed" and elevated EC readings of ~2.7mS/cm were reported. Blackhill is in the process of devising a plan to continue excavation along the buried flowline safely.The entire southeastern stormwater basin (photo #4) has been excavated and Blackhill reported that field readings within the basin were now below 1.0mS/cm. A portion of the southern stormwater conveyance channel has been lined with plastic (photo #6) and a large sump was constructed just before the stormwater basin (photo #5). Blackhill reported that water collecting in the lined sump has been field measured below 1.0mS/cm. Blackhill is currently having stormwater collected from the excavated areas and secondary containments onsite following numerous rain events over the past few days.All violations associated with the release from 4/6/2023 remain outstanding at this time against API #015-23733. I departed the site at 1000 hours.

The previously noted bare spot that was mulched and seeded in response to IR 3442875 appeared to be stable at the time of inspection (see photo 17). Violation ID: 981696
Permit API: 081-21881
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/11/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after the reported release of produced fluid to the northeast corner of Pad B and to the north stormwater channel on 12/19/22. I met with Matt Covine, Zachary Subra, and Rick Hall all of EQT during this inspection. On Pad B the sump remains installed at the northeast corner of the north stormwater channel. The fluid in the sump has an electrical conductivity (EC) of 2.07 mS/cm. A visible path was observed from the northeast edge of the sump to the farthest line of compost filter sock near the site limit-of-distance (LOD). This had not been observed in any previous inspection. Mr. Subra took an EC reading of the soil at the end of the path in front of the compost filter sock and it was 300 uS/cm. Multiple puddles of fluid were found north and northwest of the MASS. The EC of this fluid ranged from 2.62 mS/cm to 7.70 mS/cm. I took sample number 0718-199 from the puddles northwest of the mass and north of the secondary containment for the parking area of the super sucker vacuum truck.The fluid in the containment to the east of the MASS is approximately 2 mS/cm. The Department recommends emptying the containment. A line that brings fluid from the gas busters at the produced fluid offload area and puts it into the MASS appeared to still have a slow leak. A tray was underneath this area along the line which had what appeared to be an oily substance in it. The Department recommends ensuring that this does not leak onto the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming up any and all puddles found in the vicinity of the MASS until the 12/19/22 release is remediated.
